correctness.rationale: The geometric-series identity H_r(k)=(r^{2k+1}+1)/(r+1) is exact for integer r>=2 and k>=1. The seed 29 is unramified in K=Q(zeta_40,alpha), alpha^4=-5; 4^4=24=-5 modulo 29, and 29=1 mod4 gives all four distinct roots. A Frobenius class at 29 acts as exponent 29 on zeta_40 and fixes each alpha conjugate, so Chebotarev gives a positive-density set of primes q congruent 29 mod40 for which -5 is a fourth power. Since (q-1)/4 is odd, d=ord_q(-5) is odd; q>=29 makes d>=3 and a=(d-1)/2 gives q|H_5(a). q=-1 mod5 yields 5|H_q(2). For mutual divisibility of distinct odd primes p,q, (-p) and (-q) each have odd order and thus are quadratic residues; quadratic reciprocity forces p=q=1 mod4. No integrality of any full reciprocal-gcd sum follows. The concrete seed H_5(3)=13021=29*449 and H_29(2)=683705=5*136741 was independently checked. Finite testing is not the proof of positive density.

value.rationale: Reciprocal-gcd integrality work motivates a directed graph of prime-power local factors. The construction settles a naturally stated positive-density existence question for mutual divisibility with a fixed exponent in one direction, while the reciprocity restriction is a structural obstruction. This is more than a checked small witness; it neither pretends to solve full integrality nor fixes the variable exponent.
